title: A formally smooth local map of Noetherian local rings is flat with geometrically regular closed fibre
statement: Let $\varphi:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism ($\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$) of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings, let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and let $\overline B=B\otimes_Ak=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ be the closed fibre, a Noetherian $k$-algebra. If $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\overline B$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], i.e. $k'\otimes_k\overline B$ is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs, line 10081), implication (3) => (1), and its proof: Lemma 07NP (formally-smooth-flat) for flatness, Lemma 07EG (base-change-fs) for the closed fibre, Theorem 07EL (regular-fs) for (2) => (1). The source's formal smoothness is Definition 07NI with A carrying the m_A-adic topology; for a local homomorphism it is the condition of def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic (Lemma 07EC(2))

proof.text: *Flatness.* $\varphi$ is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology, so $\varphi$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-local-flat].

source.place: proof of Proposition 07NQ, 'Assume (3). By Lemma 07NP we see that A -> B is flat' (line 10099)

proof.text: *The closed fibre is a Noetherian local $k$-algebra.* Since $\varphi$ is local, the ideal $\mathfrak m_AB$ generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)$ is contained in $\mathfrak m_B$. Hence $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], and it is Noetherian as the image of the Noetherian ring $B$ under the surjection $B\to\overline B$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. The composite $A\to B\to\overline B$ kills $\mathfrak m_A$, so $\overline B$ is a $k$-algebra via $\bar a\mapsto\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m_AB$. The map $\theta:\overline B\to B\otimes_Ak$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $b\bmod\mathfrak m_AB\mapsto b\otimes1$, is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras with inverse $b\otimes\bar a\mapsto\varphi(a)b\bmod\mathfrak m_AB$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]; it is also $k$-linear for the $k$-algebra structure $\bar a\mapsto1\otimes\bar a$ on $B\otimes_Ak$, since $\theta(\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m_AB)=\varphi(a)\otimes1=1\otimes\bar a$. Finally $\theta(\mathfrak m_{\overline B})$ is the ideal of $B\otimes_Ak$ generated by $\{b\otimes1:b\in\mathfrak m_B\}$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_B(B\otimes_Ak)$, because $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$ is the ideal generated by the images of the elements of $\mathfrak m_B$ and $\theta$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: statement of Proposition 07NQ ('the special fibre B (x)_A k'), written out

proof.text: *The closed fibre is formally smooth over $k$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change] to $R=A$, $S=B$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_B$ and $R'=k$ with the quotient map $A\to k$: $S'=B\otimes_Ak$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak n'$-adic topology, $\mathfrak n'=\mathfrak m_B(B\otimes_Ak)=\theta(\mathfrak m_{\overline B})$ (Step 2). This transfers to $\overline B$ along the $k$-algebra isomorphism $\theta$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]: let $D$ be a ring with a ring map $k\to D$, $J\subseteq D$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $q:D\to D/J$ the quotient map and $g:\overline B\to D/J$ a homomorphism of $k$-algebras with $g(\mathfrak m_{\overline B}^m)=0$ for some $m\ge1$. Then $g\circ\theta^{-1}:B\otimes_Ak\to D/J$ is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras with $g\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak n'^m)=g(\mathfrak m_{\overline B}^m)=0$, as $\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak n'^m)=\mathfrak m_{\overline B}^m$; so there is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras $f':B\otimes_Ak\to D$ with $q\circ f'=g\circ\theta^{-1}$, and $f=f'\circ\theta$ is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras with $q\circ f=g$. Hence $\overline B$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology.

source.place: proof of Proposition 07NQ, 'By Lemma 07EG we see that k -> B-bar is formally smooth in the m_{B-bar}-adic topology' (lines 10099-10101)

proof.text: *Geometric regularity.* By Steps 2 and 3, $(\overline B,\mathfrak m_{\overline B})$ is a Noetherian local $k$-algebra which is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology, so by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-geometrically-regular] it is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: $k'\otimes_k\overline B$ is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$. Together with Step 1 this is the claim.
